data.narrative:
Plantd Materials is a Series B-stage housing and construction company founded by Nathan Silvernail, Huade Tan, and Josh Dorfman. The company has raised $42M to date. The comparable universe consists of two private peers—Cuby Technologies and Cover—with no directly comparable public companies identified in the sector at present.

Given the limited methodological optionality at this stage, valuation relies on stage-progression analysis, which applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement. Using total capital raised ($42M) as a proxy for implied current enterprise value, the stage-progression method yields $80M. Sensitivity around this multiplier—reflecting variation in market conditions and company-specific execution risk—produces a low bound of $68M and a high bound of $92M.

The analysis supports a median valuation of $80M with a plausible range of $68M to $92M. Key limitations include reliance on a single applicable method, a sparse peer set of only two private comparables, and absence of public market reference points. Resolution of valuation uncertainty will require either (1) revenue run-rate and margin data to support revenue multiple approaches, or (2) expansion of the private comparable set. The current range should be treated as preliminary pending deeper operational diligence.
